neighbours.label: the action inside a temporal 'as / while / until' clause of a narrative scene (fires on the clause's verb or its final word)
fire: The audience gasped as the acrobat let go of the trapeze and flew through the air.
Dogs barked in the distance as we walked home along the river.
We sat by the fire, telling stories, until the last log crumbled into ashes.
The students laughed as their coach slipped on the wet floor of the gym.
Then, as the train pulled into the station, the passengers gathered their bags.
The baby slept soundly in her crib while the storm rattled the windows.
The whole stadium roared as the runners crossed the finish line together.
Her heart pounded as she tore open the envelope from the university.
quiet: The acrobat is as strong as a weightlifter and almost as flexible as a dancer.
He worked as a guide along the river for most of his twenties.
The fireplace is made of grey stone and was built by the original owners.
The coach also serves as the school's athletic director.
The station has four platforms and a small café near the entrance.
The crib is made of solid oak and meets current safety standards.
Runners must register online and pay the entry fee by the end of March.
The envelope is the same size as a standard sheet of paper folded in half.

notes: Probe: 'as the players ran onto the pitch' 1.0, 'as the conductor raised...rang out' 0.60, 'as their teacher tried' 0.54, 'As the sun dipped...lengthened' 0.50, 'while the radio murmured' 0.45, 'until the bus...corner' 0.47; comparative/role 'as' 0.01-0.02; a 'because' narrative clause 0.25 (so near misses avoid narrative event clauses). The - pole fires on the conjunction ' as' itself.
